body.description: The message to send. The price of sending a message depends on the number of characters and the type of message. There are two types: - Standard message - Contains only characters in the GSM set, with a maximum of 160 characters. - Unicode message - Contains characters outside the GSM set, with a maximum of 70 characters. Longer messages will be sent as multiple messages (parts), but the recipient will receive them as a single long message. Visit this page to learn more about the number of characters per message, and this page to count the number of characters.

contact_id.description:
The _contact_id_ of the contact to send the message to. A _contact_id_ is connected to a _list_id_. Use the Search Contact list endpoint to view the _contact_id_ of the specified number. This parameter will be sent back to you with the response from the endpoint.

Warning:

This parameter is no longer in use.

country.description: The country code of the recipient in two-letter format (e.g. US, UK, AU, NZ, etc).

custom_string.description: A note that will be sent back to you with the response from the endpoint.

exclude_no_sender_id_recipients.description:
Used for validating whether the **Sender ID** in registered or not. You can either specify:

- **True** - It will begin sending messages without validating the Sender ID. If your contact is in a country that requires Sender ID validation, your recipient will not received it.
    
- **False** - It will only send messages if the **Sender ID** is registered.

from.description: The sender of the message. This is also referred to as the **Sender ID**. You can use: - **Shared number:** A number that is randomly selected from a pool if no number is specified. This is not available in the US and Canada. You can’t use a shared number if you have a dedicated number. - **Dedicated number:** A number you've purchased from ClickSend. You can purchase a dedicated number using the Dashboard or the [**Purchase Dedicated Number**](/accounts/sender-ids/#operation/purchase-dedicated-number) endpoint. It should be in the international format (E.164). - **Alpha tag:** A sender name, like the name of your business, used as the **Sender ID** instead of a number. Recipients cannot reply to an alpha tag. You can register an alpha tag using the dashboard or the **[Request Alpha Tag](/accounts/sender-ids/#operation/request-alpha-tag)** endpoint. Check which countries support alpha tags here. - **Own number:** Your own number that is connected to your account. Replies from recipients are sent directly to your number. You can register your own number using the dashboard or the [**Request Own Number Verification OTP**](/accounts/sender-ids/#operation/request-own-number-verification-otp) endpoint to get the _verification_id_ and OTP code needed for the [**Verify Own Number OTP**](/accounts/sender-ids/#operation/verify-own-number-otp) endpoint. This isn't available in the US and Canada. If your **Sender ID** has a different country code to the recipient’s, it'll be replaced by a local number, except in certain countries. If the sender number is blocked, a different number will replace it.

from_email.description: The email address to which replies should be emailed to. If omitted, the reply will be emailed back to the user who sent the outgoing SMS.

list_id.description: The _list_id_ of the contact list to send the message to. Use the [**View Contact List**](/contacts/lists/#operation/view-list-contacts) endpoint to see your contact lists. You can also use the other [lists endpoints](/contacts/lists/) to create and manage your contact list. You need to provide the _to_ parameter or the _list_id_ parameter.

schedule.description: The time you want the message to be sent. It should be in Unix format.

source.description: The source of the request. For example, the name of your application. It's used to identify messages sent from various applications.

to.description:
The phone number of the recipient. It should be in the international format (E.164). You can send to a contact list using the _list_id_ parameter. You need to provide the _to_ parameter or the _list_id_ parameter.

Note:

To send SMS overseas, enable the global sending feature on your account either through the Dashboard, or by contacting customer support.
